newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo stocks rebound, seen holding upward path.
newsitem.headline: Oslo stocks rebound, seen holding upward path.

text.p: Norwegian shares rebounded on Monday with blue chips leading the market up from pre-weekend losses.

Forestry group Norske Skog and shipbuilding and engineering group Kvaerner were two of the best performers and brokers said they expected the market to continue to gain and to hit new all-time highs before year end.

"Sentiment is very strong. Interest rates are low and there's a lot of cash coming into the market from private and fund investors," said one dealer. "There's no other alternative at the moment if you want some yield on your money."
Oslo's Total share index climbed 1.48 percent to close at 942.93 points in turnover of 778 million crowns.

Kvaerner generated 139 million crowns of trade and gained 11 crowns to 287. Brokers said the stock was buoyed by weekend reports that it had won a 2.7 billion crown contract to build a floating production ship for Woodside Petroleum of Australia.
Kvaerner on Monday said it had not signed a contract, but did not rule out the possibility of an announcement soon.
Norske Skog climbed 10 crowns to 207 crowns after Sweden's Stora announced price increases. Skog said it expected pulp prices to rise early next year.
